title: Anchored Response Contract and Deployment Playbook for Cache- and Quant-Sensitive Models
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This playbook defines the Anchored Response Contract (ARC) used to validate model output consistency across stash/kv-cache boundaries and quantized execution paths. ARC is intended for production rollouts of latency- and cost-sensitive models where caching and quantization changes can cause subtle regressions (semantic drift, hallucination amplification, or tokenization sensitivity).

Scope and intended audience:
- Applies to models promoted for real-time host inference (hosted, dedicated, private) where KV cache and quantized variants are in the serving mix.
- Primary readers: model owners, applied ML engineers, runtime engineers, SRE oncall, and release managers.

Goals:
1) Provide a small, high-signal anchored dataset and measurable contract for behavioral stability after changes to caching, quantization, or kernel selection.
2) Define monitoring signals and thresholds that can be automated in CI/canary to permit safe progressive rollout.
3) Supply an operator playbook for fast triage and rollback when the contract fails.

Definitions:
- Anchor: a short set (typically 50–200) of model inputs with human-validated expected semantics. Anchors include prompts that are known to be cache-sensitive (prefix repeats, long-term context re-use), ambiguity probes (disambiguation tasks), and safety-critical examples.
- ARC: the numeric contract evaluating response similarity and quality delta between a golden baseline (unquantized, warm cache) and the test variant (quantized, cold/warm cache combos).
- Golden profile: the baseline model + runtime (float16/FP32, standard kernels, warmed KV cache).

Contract metrics and thresholds (recommended defaults):
- Semantic similarity (embed_cosine): median >= 0.92 and 10th percentile >= 0.86. Measure using the production embedding model used for downstream ranking.
- Token-level log-prob KL (avg_token_kl): <= 0.08 across anchor set.
- Edit distance normalized (norm_levenshtein): mean <= 0.15.
- Deterministic exact match for canonical-answer slices: >= 0.95 for high-precision prompts (FAQ/format responses).
- Safety sentinel pass-rate (safety_gate): >= 0.995 (binary).
- Latency SLO delta: p95 latency increase <= 10% for quant+cache warm path versus golden.

Thresholds are tunable per workload; teams must record final values in the model’s certification ticket.

Anchor construction guidelines:
- Size: 50–200 inputs, stratified by slice: 40% cache-sensitive, 30% short-turn QA, 20% long-context summarization, 10% safety-critical.
- Labeling: each anchor example must include human-validated expected intents/outcomes and a short rubric (1–3 lines) describing acceptable variation.
- Ownership: model owner owns anchor curation; evaluator team performs periodic review (quarterly) for drift.

Evaluation modes and required gates:
1) CI smoke (fast): run anchor set with 10-sample temperature seeds; compute semantic similarity and safety sentinel. Gate: fail if median embed_cosine < specified threshold or any safety sentinel fails.
2) Shadow canary (mixed): run anchored traffic in shadow for 24–72 hours across cold/warm cache mixes and quant variants. Gate: pass semantic and safety thresholds; monitor latency delta and error rates.
3) Progressive rollout: 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% over 24–72 hour windows. At each step, recompute ARC metrics and check trend constraints (no monotonic degradation > 2% per step).

Operational telemetry to capture (minimum):
- Per-request: variant_id, cache_state (cold/warm), quant_profile, seq_len, p95_latency_ms, token_count.
- Quality: embed_cosine, avg_token_kl, norm_levenshtein, sentinel_flags.
- Business signals: downstream conversion/CTR, human-annotator flags for sampled requests.

Example ARC report table (ASCII):
| metric                    | golden  | quantized-warm | quantized-cold | delta | pass |
|---------------------------|---------|----------------|----------------|-------|------|
| median_embed_cosine       | 0.940   | 0.927          | 0.915          | -0.025| FAIL |
| p10_embed_cosine          | 0.890   | 0.872          | 0.854          | -0.036| FAIL |
| mean_norm_levenshtein     | 0.08    | 0.10           | 0.12           | +0.04 | FAIL |
| avg_token_kl              | 0.03    | 0.05           | 0.07           | +0.04 | FAIL |
| safety_gate               | 1.0     | 1.0            | 0.99           | -0.01 | PASS |
| p95_latency_ms            | 45      | 40             | 62             | +17   | FAIL |

Interpretation: failing metrics in quantized-cold indicate cache-priming interaction amplified by quantization. Follow triage flow below.

Deployment and triage flow (numbered playbook):
1) Pre-deploy checklist (owner/model):
   a) Anchor set created and reviewed.
   b) Baseline golden run logged with artifact-id and seed.
   c) Telemetry hooks in tracing and metrics are enabled (variant_id, cache_state).
   d) Canary policy configured in deployment manifest (see example).
2) CI smoke: automated ARC check. If fail -> block and notify owner.
3) Shadow canary run: run for 24–72 hours, gather ARC. If any metric fails -> escalate to oncall and pause rollout.
4) On-failure quick triage (first 30 minutes):
   a) Confirm which slices fail (cache-sensitive? long-context?)
   b) Re-run failing anchors under golden config to verify artifact mismatch.
   c) If failure only in cold cache: consider increasing warmup prefetch, or enable prefix caching for identified slices.
   d) If failure correlated with quant_profile: test alternative quant profile (e.g., int8->q4 or mixed-precision) and compare.
5) Remediation options (ranked):
   a) Abort rollout and revert to previous deployment.
   b) Route affected slices to golden variant via routing rules (per-route routing).
   c) Apply a quant-fallback policy for specific endpoints or tenant classes.
   d) Adjust batch/kv-cache priming policy to reduce cold-cache exposure.
6) Post-mortem: create an incident ticket including ARC report, failing anchor list, and remediation chosen. Attach model artifacts and runtime kernel logs.

Example deployment manifest fragment (text YAML):
---
canary_policy:
  steps: [5, 20, 50, 100]
  wait_hours: 12
  guardrails:
    arc_checks: true
    arc_thresholds:
      median_embed_cosine: 0.92
      p10_embed_cosine: 0.86
      avg_token_kl: 0.08
      safety_gate: 0.995
quant_profiles:
  - name: q4_legacy
  - name: q4_hybrid
cache_policies:
  warmup_strategy: prefetch
  prefetch_keys: 3
---

Troubleshooting playbook (common failure signatures and first actions):
- Signature: embed_cosine drop concentrated on cache-sensitive anchors -> first action: re-run anchors with forced warm cache; if warm passes and cold fails, increase prefetch or reduce cache TTL for the affected prefix.
- Signature: increased avg_token_kl with minimal embed change -> first action: reproduce with different random seeds and compare token-level logprobs to find diverging tokens; test alternate quant profile.
- Signature: p95 latency spike under quantized path -> first action: capture kernel-level profiling (kernel selection differences), check batching and kernel fallback events; if kernels are slower at short seq_len, consider changing kernel selection or use mixed-precision path.
- Signature: safety sentinel flip on a small subset -> first action: isolate examples, send to safety team for rapid adjudication, immediately route matching slices to golden variant until cleared.

Automations and CI integrations (recommended):
- Add ARC checks to merge-gate for model-promote PRs. Provide a precomputed golden artifact and a small fast-anchor run in CI to reduce friction.
- Build a nightly ARC monitor that samples production anchors and records trend lines (rolling 7d).
- Add automatic partial routing rule generation: when anchor-specific regression is detected, generate a routing suggestion PR (route matching prefix -> golden).

Ownership and SLAs:
- Model owner: anchor curation, initial CI integration, and first-response triage.
- Runtime team: ensure telemetry and kernel traces are available, own quant profile rollout automation.
- SRE/oncall: initial triage for canary failures and rollback, own runbook enactment.
- Safety/evals: review any sentinel failures and label anchors as needed.

Key links and artifacts (internal):
- ARC evaluation harness repository: git+ssh://git.redwood/arc-harness.git
- Anchor storage and manifest: s3://redwood-eval/anchors/{model_name}/{anchor_id}.tar.gz
- Regression triage playbook: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/model-regression-forensics-playbook-2026
- Shadow-to-prod continuity guide: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/shadow-to-prod-eval-continuity-guidelines-2026

Appendix A — Example anchor entry format (JSON text):
{
  "id": "anchor-042",
  "prompt": "Summarize the following conversation keeping names anonymized:",
  "expected_rubric": "Preserve action items and timeline; omit PII. Acceptable paraphrase, not required exact wording.",
  "slices": ["long_context", "privacy_sensitive"],
  "golden_artifact": "model-2025-11-06:artifact-9"
}

Appendix B — Example quick-check CLI (pseudo):
# run fast ARC locally against quant profile
redwood-eval run-arc --model model-2025-11-06 --quant q4_hybrid --anchors anchors/anchor-042.json --seed 42 --output report.json

Notes and caveats:
- ARC is not a replacement for full eval-suite promotion gates. It is a targeted, high-signal contract designed to catch behavioral regressions introduced by runtime changes that are hard to observe via token-cost or latency-only checks.
- Teams with high-variance workloads should increase anchor size and tighten thresholds for safety-critical routes.
- Be mindful of privacy when curating anchors; prefer synthetic or redacted production examples and follow the anchor retention policy.
